title: A data dictionary template for Mac: how to build one for data governance
metaTitle: Data dictionary template for Mac: guide for data governance analysts
description: Learn how to build a robust data dictionary template on your Mac to manage metadata and governance standards effectively.
intro: A data dictionary template helps you standardize definitions and metadata across your organization. You can build a custom data dictionary template on your Mac using tools like Excel or Notion to keep your data definitions clear and accessible.
tldr: Use a structured data dictionary template to track field names, data types, and business definitions.
Data governance analysts spend significant time on administrative tasks, making documentation templates essential for efficiency.
Lazur helps you manage your documentation workflow by providing quick access to notes and drafting definitions.
Keep your data dictionary in a shared space to ensure all stakeholders follow the same standards.

blocks.text: Why you need a standard data dictionary template

Data governance relies on clear communication. When you use a consistent data dictionary template, you reduce the time spent answering repetitive questions about data fields. It serves as the single source of truth for your team. You should define column names, data types, and business logic for every dataset you manage.
Structuring your data dictionary for maximum impact

Your template should be simple. Start with a spreadsheet or a database table. Include columns for field name, business definition, data type, and the owner of the data. This structure helps you map lineage and ensure compliance with internal policies.

items: Field Name: The technical name used in the database.
Business Definition: A plain language description for stakeholders.
Data Type: Integer, string, date, or custom format.
Data Owner: The person responsible for the data quality.
Security Classification: Public, internal, or restricted.

blocks.text: Managing metadata documentation on your Mac

You likely use apps like Excel, Notion, or TablePlus for your work. On a Mac, you can organize these with tools like SupaSidebar to keep your documentation tabs accessible. When you need to draft a definition, hold the fn key to dictate text directly into your document. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your focus on the data.
If you are working with sensitive data, always follow your employer's specific rules regarding data handling and storage. Do not store sensitive information in public cloud templates.

blocks.text: Common mistakes in data dictionary maintenance

One common mistake is building a template that is too complex. If it takes too long to fill out, your team will stop using it. Keep your entries concise. Another error is failing to update the dictionary when the underlying data schema changes. Set a recurring task in your calendar to audit your dictionary entries every month.
Using Lazur to support your documentation workflow

Lazur acts as a bridge between your tools. If you are stuck on a complex SQL query in DBeaver, hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about the syntax. If you need to draft a message to a data steward about a definition, use the dictation feature to write it quickly. Lazur helps you stay in the flow by handling the administrative parts of your job.
How to choose the right tool for your dictionary

Notion is great for collaborative documentation and linking to policies. Excel or Google Sheets are better if you need to perform calculations or manage large lists of metadata. Evaluate your team's needs before choosing. If you need to share the dictionary, prioritize apps that support real-time collaboration.
Next steps for your data governance strategy

Once your template is ready, socialize it with your team. Get feedback on whether the fields are useful and easy to understand. A data dictionary is a living document. It should grow and change as your data environment matures. Monitor how often your team refers to the dictionary to measure its success.

faq.question: What should I include in a data dictionary template?
faq.answer: Include the field name, business definition, data type, owner, and security classification. This provides enough context for most users.

faq.question: Can I use Excel for my data dictionary?
faq.answer: Yes, Excel is a standard tool for ad-hoc data management. It works well for smaller datasets and is easy to share with colleagues.

faq.question: How often should I update my data dictionary?
faq.answer: Update it whenever the data schema changes. Conduct a full audit of your documentation at least once per month to ensure accuracy.
